research_mode: official Home Office primary statistical bulletin; fail-closed limitations; no parcel score or business result

sources.name: Non-victim-based charge time
verified_claims: Charge or summons outcomes for non-victim-based offences took a median of 40 days.
limitations: Processing time does not represent parcel-level public-safety conditions.

sources.name: Drug offence charge time
verified_claims: Drug offence charge or summons outcomes took 53 days, down from 62 days.
limitations: Drug offence volumes and outcomes are highly influenced by enforcement activity.

sources.name: Possession of weapons charge time
verified_claims: Possession of weapons charge or summons outcomes took 18 days, down from 22 days.
limitations: This outcome timing does not locate offences or quantify local exposure.

sources.name: Public order charge time
verified_claims: Public order charge or summons outcomes took 28 days, down from 36 days.
limitations: Changes can reflect operational and case-mix effects.

sources.name: Firearm-involved charge or summons rate
verified_claims: Around 12.9% of offences involving a firearm resulted in a charge or summons, up from 12.0%.
limitations: Firearm involvement is a cross-cutting subset and the rate is not a local risk score.

sources.name: Knife-enabled charge or summons rate
verified_claims: Around 13.0% of knife-enabled offences resulted in a charge or summons, up from 11.5%.
limitations: Knife-enabled outcomes must not be interpreted as exact-location evidence.

sources.name: Knife and non-knife charge comparison
verified_claims: The knife-enabled charge or summons rate of 13.0% was higher than the 7.5% rate for equivalent offences not involving a knife.
limitations: Differences may reflect offence seriousness, evidence, and investigation selection.

sources.name: Police-force coverage
verified_claims: The bulletin covers all territorial police forces in England and Wales and British Transport Police.
limitations: National coverage does not guarantee uniform recording quality across forces.

sources.name: Current outcomes framework
verified_claims: The current crime outcomes framework was introduced in April 2013, replacing the narrower detections framework.
limitations: Long-term comparisons across framework changes require caution.

sources.name: Year-end snapshot status
verified_claims: The main outcomes data are a snapshot of the case status of offences recorded during the year ending March 2026.
limitations: Cases still open at the snapshot date can change outcome later.

sources.name: Outcome revisions
verified_claims: Police forces submit revised data as investigations are completed, so previously published outcomes can be revised.
limitations: First-release figures are not final for complex offences.

sources.name: One recorded outcome per crime
verified_claims: For statistical purposes, every recorded crime is assigned one outcome type.
limitations: One outcome category does not capture every investigative action or later justice result.

sources.name: Full outcome open data
verified_claims: Open data tables publish the full range of police outcome types beyond grouped bulletin categories.
limitations: Open data availability does not remove disclosure, quality, or comparability limitations.

sources.name: Alternative offence charges for victim-based offences
verified_claims: Approximately 12.6% of victim-based charge outcomes related to an alternative offence to the one originally recorded.
limitations: The centrally held data cannot identify the specific alternative offence charged.

sources.name: Alternative offence charges for non-victim-based offences
verified_claims: Approximately 4.8% of non-victim-based charge outcomes related to an alternative offence.
limitations: Alternative-offence rates should not be used to infer local offending patterns.

sources.name: Victim-based offence volume
verified_claims: Around 4.4 million victim-based offences were recorded in the 12 months to March 2026, 2% fewer than the previous year.
limitations: Recorded volume is affected by reporting and recording practices.

sources.name: Victim-based offences under investigation
verified_claims: At year-end, 6.9% of victim-based offences remained under investigation, down from 7.9%.
limitations: Open-case shares depend on offence complexity and recording date.

sources.name: Victim-based charge volume
verified_claims: The volume of charge or summons outcomes for victim-based offences rose 12.8%, from 345,521 to 389,728.
limitations: Outcome volume is not directly comparable with crime prevalence.

sources.name: Victim-based charge proportion
verified_claims: The victim-based charge or summons proportion increased from 6.3% to 7.3%.
limitations: Year-end proportions are incomplete where many investigations remain open.

sources.name: Victim-based charge long-term trend
verified_claims: The victim-based charge or summons proportion fell from 11.1% in the year ending March 2016 to 4.6% in the year ending March 2022 before the recent rise.
limitations: Framework, recording, case-mix, and investigation changes limit causal interpretation.
